'''David Mervyn Blow''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FInstP}}<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Henderson | first1 = R. | last2 = Franks | first2 = N. P. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.2008.0022  | doi-access = free| title = David Mervyn Blow. 27 June 1931 -- 8 June 2004 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 55 | pages = 13–35 | year = 2009 | s2cid = 56616438 }}</ref> (27 June 1931 – 8 June 2004)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Blow, Prof. David Mervyn | id = U7898 | type=was|year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U7898 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref><ref name=nytimes/><ref name=grauniad/> was a British [[biophysicist]]. He was best known for the development of [[X-ray crystallography]], a technique used to determine the [[molecule|molecular structure]]s of tens of thousands of biological molecules.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Vrielink | first1 = Alice | title = David Mervyn Blow | doi = 10.1063/1.1897573 | journal = [[Physics Today]] | volume = 58 | issue = 3 | pages = 88–89| year = 2005 |bibcode = 2005PhT....58c..88V | doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Blow was born in [[Birmingham]], England. He was educated at [[Kingswood School]] in [[Bath, Somerset]] and the [[University of Cambridge]] where he won a scholarship to [[Corpus Christi College, Cambridge]]. His PhD was awarded in 1958 for X-ray analysis of [[haemoglobin]] supervised by [[Max Perutz]] at the [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology|MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB)]].<ref name=mervphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=http://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/34896765?style=html|title=X-ray analysis of haemoglobin: determination of phase angles by isomorphous substitution|first=David Mervyn|last=Blow|year=1958|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.596730}}|website=copac.jisc.ac.uk|oclc=879392023|access-date=15 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216025022/http://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/34896765?style=html|archive-date=16 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Henderson |first1=R. |last2=Franks |first2=N. P. |date=2009 |title=David Mervyn Blow. 27 June 1931 — 8 June 2004 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2008.0022 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |language=en |volume=55 |pages=13–35 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2008.0022  |doi-access=free|s2cid=56616438 |issn=0080-4606|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Following graduation from Cambridge, Blow spent two years at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) and the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH) funded by the [[Fulbright Foundation]]<ref name=whoswho/>

In 1954, he met [[Max Perutz]];<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Blow | first1 = David Mervyn | author-link = David Mervyn Blow| doi = 10.1098/rsbm.2004.0016 | title = Max Ferdinand Perutz OM CH CBE. 19 May 1914 – 6 February 2002: Elected F.R.S. 1954 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 50 | pages = 227–256 | year = 2004 | pmid =  15768489| jstor = 4140521| s2cid = 73986989 | doi-access = free }}</ref> they began to study a new technique wherein [[X-ray]]s would be passed through a [[protein]] sample at the [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]]. This eventually led to the creation of a three-dimensional structure of [[haemoglobin]].<ref name="RossmannBlow1962">{{cite journal|last1=Rossmann|first1=M. G.|last2=Blow|first2=D. M.|title=The detection of sub-units within the crystallographic asymmetric unit|journal=[[Acta Crystallographica]]|volume=15|issue=1|year=1962|pages=24–31|issn=0365-110X|doi=10.1107/S0365110X62000067|bibcode=1962AcCry..15...24R }}</ref> Blow was appointed professor of biophysics at [[Imperial College London]] in 1977. His doctoral students include [[Richard Henderson (biologist)|Richard Henderson]],<ref name=hendphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|url=http://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=44CAM_ALMA21429746340003606&context=L&vid=44CAM_PROD&search_scope=SCOP_CAM_ALL&tab=cam_lib_coll&lang=en_US|title=X-ray analysis of α-chymotrysin: substrate and inhibitor binding|first= Richard|last=Henderson|year=1969|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.458866}}|publisher=University of Cambridge|oclc=500470310}}</ref><ref name=tls>{{cite web|first=Jim|last=Al-Khalili|author-link=Jim Al-Khalili|year=2018|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b09r4c8f|title=Richard Henderson zooms in on the molecules of life|publisher=BBC}}</ref> [[Paul Sigler]],<ref name="blowacademictruee" /> and [[Alice Vrielink]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Vrielink|first=Alice|date=2014-07-03|title=David Blow (1931-2004) - A Remberance|url=http://www.amercrystalassn.org/documents/newsletterarchive/2004Winter.pdf|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-14|website=American Crystallographic Association|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703002900/http://www.amercrystalassn.org/documents/newsletterarchive/2004Winter.pdf|archive-date=3 July 2014}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Blow was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1972|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1972]]. He was awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]] in 1987.<ref name=whoswho/>

==Personal life==
Blow married Mavis Sears in 1955, and they had two children, a son Julian and a daughter Elizabeth.<ref name=whoswho/><ref name=grauniad /> He died of lung cancer at the age of 72, in [[Appledore, Torridge]] (near [[Bideford]]), [[Devon]].<ref name=nytimes>{{cite news |first=Jeremy |last=Pearce |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/07/19/science/19blow.html |date=19 July 2007 |title=David Blow, 72; Briton Developed Method to Study Proteins |newspaper=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref name=grauniad>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2004/jun/25/guardianobituaries.obituaries |title=David Blow Pioneering scientist in protein crystallography |first=Michael |last=Rossmann |date=25 June 2004 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>
